children: The rupee gained further on Friday, November 20, after the currency opened flat on Thursday. The market is pricing in Fed rate hikes, even as the US dollar strengthens.
The Indian currency opened at 93.20 per US dollar, marginally stronger than Thursday's (November 19) close of 93.29, marking a leap of 0.070 paise.
The Rupee has opened positive on three occasions, and flat yesterday. This week so far, the rupee has gained 1.04 paise.

The influx of foreign capital into equity markets has also reduced pressure on the central bank to defend the rupee, enabling it to sharply scale back dollar sales after months of heavy intervention, a Reuters report said.

According to the same report, traders and analysts are monitoring for signs that exporters are converting more of their dollar earnings, alongside continued portfolio inflows, to assess how much further the rupee could strengthen.

So far, corporate activity appears mixed across lenders: some report increased exporter participation, while others continue to see elevated importer hedging and exporters largely staying on the sidelines.

The US dollar was on track for a fourth consecutive weekly advance on Friday, November 20, as demand associated with Anthropic’s stock market debut strengthened expectations that the Federal Reserve would continue raising interest rates.
After two good sessions, the markets are now looking to maintain the momentum. However, GIFT Nifty so far has indicated a gap-down start to the day's proceedings, as Nifty aims for 25,500.

Asian markets have slumped steeply. Japan suffered the steepest declines, with the Nikkei 225 falling 4.54% and the broader Topix dropping 2.75%. South Korea’s Kospi slid 4.74%, while Hang Seng futures edged down 0.2%.
Anthropic shares started trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on Thursday in the largest public debut on record, then rose 17% on their first day.
Another key aspect that dictates the movement in the currency market: oil appears to be steadying above the $90 mark, trading around $93 per barrel.

title: Rupee today: Indian currency opens at 93.20, gains over ₹1 this week against US dollar
